Lisa Yan, Chris Piech, Mehran Sahami, and Jerry Cain, CS109, Spring 2024
Memorylessness: Hurry Up and Wait
A continuous probability distribution is said to be memoryless if a 
random variable 𝑋 on that probability distribution satisfies the following for 
all 𝑠, 𝑡≥ 0:
𝑃𝑋≥𝑠+ 𝑡 | 𝑋≥𝑠= 𝑃𝑋≥𝑡
32
• Here, 𝑠 represents the time you’ve already spent waiting.
• The above states that after you’ve waited 𝑠 time units, the probability 
you’ll need to wait an additional 𝑡 time units is equal to the probability 
you’d have to wait 𝑡 time units without having waited those 𝑠 time units 
in the first place.
• Example: If train arrival is guided by a memoryless random variable, the 
fact that you’ve waited 15 minutes doesn’t obligate the train to arrive 
any faster!

Lisa Yan, Chris Piech, Mehran Sahami, and Jerry Cain, CS109, Spring 2024

A continuous probability distribution is said to be memoryless if a

𝑃𝑋≥𝑠+ 𝑡 | 𝑋≥𝑠= 𝑃𝑋≥𝑡
